commands.help: Release a needs-approval hold (records approval_granted).
Attach to a running agent's live event stream.
Append the current chain head to the anchors file (pure-local; no git).
Export the audit trail to JSON or CSV (chronological).
Explicitly recover or adopt one verified ledger; never merge chains.
Show the current effective policy, or resolve a retained policy hash.
Show recent audit events (oldest first).
Verify audit-log chain integrity (exit 0 ok / 1 tamper / 2 cannot-run).
Snapshot the dispatch.db record (+ config) into a portable archive.
Attest kew still reads fresh vendor CLI output correctly.
Dispatch CI failure auto-fix for a GitHub Actions run.
Find and fix orphaned label states left after a crash.
Show the runtime configuration and, optionally, its winning sources.
Watch for assign-to-kew delegation and claim → dispatch it (foreground).
Deny a needs-approval hold (records approval_declined; parks the issue).
Dispatch an issue. With --loop, supervise the runner as a first-class loop.
Run local environment diagnostics.
Confirm one exact execution boundary with a single bounded provider call.
Drive every active epic of the project from one supervised process.
Admit no new work — dispatch, review or remediation — until `kew drive release`. Every epic keeps ticking, so running work finishes and merges. The hold is kept in the ledger and outlives the drive.
Install the drive as a launchd agent (macOS): it starts at login and restarts when it exits abnormally. `kew drive stop` still ends it.
Stop ticking EPIC (or every epic) until `kew drive resume`; a running tick finishes. The pause is kept in the ledger and outlives the drive.
Lift `kew drive hold`: the next tick admits under the cap again.
Tick EPIC again — or, with no EPIC, lift every pause.
Print the running drive's heartbeat: its stage, rotation and last tick per epic. Exits 1 when no drive runs or its heartbeat has stalled.
Stop the running drive after its current tick — or, with EPIC, stop ticking that epic for the rest of this drive's run.
Remove the launchd agent `kew drive install` wrote; a drive it started is stopped by launchd.
Abandon preserved work and return the node for fresh dispatch.
Record an amendment to NAME's node ITEM's acceptance contract.
Run ONE tick of the epic driver: dispatch ready nodes, merge approved PRs, and print the resulting status.
Retire a finished or abandoned epic from the active views.
Continue one positively-orphaned dirty epic worktree in place.
Export the epic DAG as a Mermaid or DOT diagram.
Say the epic's loop is alive and waiting on purpose.
Merge ONE READY node of an epic, on the operator's own authority.
Turn an implementation plan into a drivable epic (governed planning run).

Re-admit a FAILED epic node WITHOUT deleting its run history: clear its `agent-failed` label, release any stale reservation, and record a retry marker so the driver's overlay treats the stale failure run(s) as superseded instead of discarding them — cost/token history stays intact for `kew report`.

Poll the epic driver (advance every `--interval` seconds) until COMPLETE or STALLED. Never loops on STALLED — exits non-zero so an operator can intervene. With ``--all``, advances every known epic round-robin in the one loop until ALL are terminal.

Send a READY epic node back for remediation — the operator's NEEDS_CHANGES. Records a NEEDS_CHANGES round against the head the node's READY verdict stands on, which must still be the pull request's head on GitHub, attested with you as its actor and the reason file's text as its one finding. The drive's next tick reads the node as remediating and runs the remediation under the node's own item id, so the drive keeps owning the node — unlike `kew review <PR>` or a commit of your own on the agent branch.

Summarize epic progress: node counts by status, the ready frontier, stuck nodes + blast radius, and the terminal signal — including `awaiting_merges` when a human merge is all that is left. Never dispatches or merges.
Return an archived epic to the active views.

Release a driver hold on an epic node — the operator counterpart to the driver's own hold bookkeeping. Clears the `epic_holds` row for <name>/<item> via the store API and, on a GitHub tracker, strips the stale `pr-pending-review` label (mirror of the manual unwedge playbook); a non-github tracker owns node state in the tracker itself, so no label is touched. Names the cleared reason + held-since time; exits 2 when no hold exists for that epic/item.
Validate the epic DAG (cycles, dangling deps, self-edges).
Emit one structured event per epic state that needs a person.
Export run history to JSON, CSV, or a model-eol inventory.
Repair a run left awaiting host publication after out-of-band publication.
List what closed work left on disk; --apply removes it.
Attest the control plane is functioning: meter, budgets, audit, runner.
Run kew's checked-in provisioning recipe on a host and record its versions.
Drop a named holder's lease on a host, by hand.
Ingest a Claude Code OTLP/JSON metrics export into the run store.
Run a loopback OTLP/HTTP receiver for Claude Code metrics.
Write kew.toml from detection, flags and answers, then run setup and doctor.
Stop one run through its authenticated process identity.
Pause a running loop by stopping its current step.
Resume a needs_human / budget_limited loop with guidance.
Refuse a hand merge while the head's newest review verdict stands against it.
Show every live merge claim.
Give the head back to the drive.
Extend your live claim by another 15 minutes.
Claim a PR head for 15 minutes; renew it every 5 while you verify.
Queue a READY PR head behind every entry already queued.
Show the queue in the order it merges.
Take a PR out of the queue.
Verify and merge the head of the queue once, as the drive does.
Check configured and explicit model ids against the curated registry.

Authorize this item's no-change outcome and synchronize it to its source.
Refuse this item's no-change outcome. Closes nothing, unblocks nothing.

Re-run a synchronization that held, for an outcome already decided.
Print an item's recorded plan: its sha, source and acceptance criteria.
Activate a proposed profile version, retiring the one it replaces.
Decline a proposed profile version; what the role runs is unchanged.

Propose an addendum for a role; it changes nothing until approved.

Release one runner's quota hold now, before the provider's reset.
Move the ledger's rows from an old repository slug to project.repo.

Export a self-contained evidence pack (HTML or JSON twin).
Write each console feature's build history, and a cleaned run export.

Restore a backup archive into the configured log directory.
Clear the fleet-stop latch and re-enable dispatch.
Gather PR review comments and dispatch agent to address them.
Take the next ready issue from the queue and dispatch the configured runner.
The newest run requests and what the drive did with each.
Queue COMMAND for the running `kew drive`, which runs it as you.
One run request in full. Exits 1 when there is no such request.

Show dispatch queue status.

Compare a fixed corpus through direct and managed passthrough modes.
